about.title: Scotts Valley Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Scotts Valley is home to just under 12,000 people in Santa Cruz County, and when a family here loses someone, the absence is felt well beyond one household. Public records show 16 injury collisions in 2025 on local roads, with Mt Hermon Road, Scotts Valley Drive, SR-17, and Glenwood Drive carrying the largest share of reported crashes. No traffic deaths were logged in the city that year, but wrongful death claims in California reach beyond the roadway. A fall on unsafe property, a defective product, or a crash on the commute over the hill can leave a family facing the same hard questions. California limits who may file: a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public entity is involved. We handle wrongful death claims on a contingency basis, meaning you pay no fee unless we recover for your family.

whyChoose.title: What a Scotts Valley Family Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Who is allowed to bring the claim
items.desc: California gives a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to file, with certain dependents and heirs able to step in when they are not present. We can sort out who belongs on the claim before anything is submitted.

items.title: The clock runs from the date of death
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions must be filed within two years of the date your loved one passed. If a city, county, or state agency such as Caltrans is involved, the window to give notice is far shorter, so early review matters.

items.title: Civil losses are counted separately from any criminal case
items.desc: A wrongful death claim is a civil action that can proceed whether or not prosecutors file charges. It seeks funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance.

items.question: My spouse died in a crash on SR-17 near Scotts Valley. Does it matter that the highway is state-maintained?
items.answer: It can. If part of the claim involves the condition of the roadway itself, a government entity may be a defendant, and California requires a formal claim to that agency on a much shorter timeline than the standard two years. A claim against the other driver still follows the usual rules. We can look at both paths at once so nothing is missed.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil matter and runs on its own track, separate from anything the district attorney does. Your family does not need a conviction to move forward, and waiting for the criminal case could eat into your filing deadline. We begin gathering evidence right away while the criminal case unfolds.

items.question: Do you charge our family anything for a consultation?
items.answer: Nothing at all. We handle wrongful death claims on a contingency basis, which means we are paid only if there is a recovery for your family.
